I have farmed a long time, so I do not start from fancy ideas. I start from what worked on my own land last year and what I saw on nearby fields. My place is 10.9 mu, not tiny but not big either, so every bag of fertilizer still matters. I will keep more land in stevia because that is the crop I count on, then I will spread the rest across wheat, maize, cotton, and a little millet so I am not putting all my money in one place.

For wheat, I will keep it steady and not cut fertilizer too hard, because weak wheat shows fast and then there is no way to fully get it back. I will plough it, put the base fertilizer in before sowing, and give it about 12 kg nitrogen, 6 kg phosphorus, and 4 kg potassium per mu. With well water, I will give it 3 irrigations if the season is normal. I will spray about 2 times, mainly for weeds and then disease or aphids if they come. If the weather does not turn against me, I will look for around 450 kg per mu.

For maize, I will use hybrid seed because that is what people around me plant when they want a steady ear and better yield. I will not starve maize, because maize eats fertilizer. I will give about 14 kg nitrogen, 5 kg phosphorus, and 5 kg potassium per mu, with 2 irrigations. I will spray 2 times. I will use rotary tillage because it is quicker and costs less labor than deep ploughing every time. If it stands well, I will count on around 500 kg per mu.

For millet, I will keep just a small patch. Millet can handle poorer ground better than maize, so I will not spend too much there. I will use improved seed if I can get the same kind that did well for others nearby. I will give about 8 kg nitrogen, 4 kg phosphorus, and 3 kg potassium per mu, 1 irrigation, and 1 spray. I will use rotary tillage and aim for around 280 kg per mu.

For cotton, I will not go light on fertilizer because once cotton gets weak, the bolls do not come well. I will use improved seed, plough the land, and put about 15 kg nitrogen, 6 kg phosphorus, and 6 kg potassium per mu. Cotton needs watching, so I will plan 3 irrigations and around 4 pesticide sprays, because insects can eat profit fast. If management goes smoothly, I will look for about 320 kg per mu.

For stevia, I will put the biggest area there. Stevia needs careful feeding but not wild spending. I will follow the way I have seen work: enough base fertilizer, then topdressing when it starts pushing. I will use improved planting material, plough the field, and give about 13 kg nitrogen, 7 kg phosphorus, and 7 kg potassium per mu. With my well, I will plan 4 irrigations. I will spray about 3 times, mostly to keep leaf damage down. If the stand is even, I will expect about 350 kg per mu.
